newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JAN 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS - JAN 20.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Prime Minister Costas Simitis is expected to make overtures to leading members of ruling party PASOK in an effort to create a team which will take the lead on crucial issues. In this way, Simitis hopes to overturn charges made last week that he governs alone and to involve all in the renaissance of the party.

--Teachers strike today, saying present bread and butter issues are more pressing than Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis's plans to overhaul secondary and tertiary education. Arsenis will meet with university heads on Saturday in an effort to shape his proposals.
--There was tension at the country's major port of Piraeus overnight as striking dockworkers and farmers wanting to load produce came face to face.
--The government faces a double challenge from ports and schools, but is determined not to give in. The stand-off at the ports however is worrying.

--The latest wave of labour unrest poses a serious challenge to the prime minister and the ruling party. Dockworkers yesterday received the message that if they did not relent the government would step in to ensure farm produce was moved.

--Former defence minister Arsenis, currently on a visit to Cyprus, says Simitis's recent statements on relations between Athens and Nicosia decides was a recipe for "national disaster" and criticising those who place too much faith in US mediation.
--The government is using one group against the other to deal with the latest round of strike action. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
